name: Goblin
description: Tsukuyomi could turn a monster face-down, allowing its controller to reuse Flip Effects or attack a monster with low DEF. Thousand-Eyes Restrict was a particularly effective partner because it could repeatedly absorb opposing monsters.

defining_cards.name: Tsukuyomi
defining_cards.why: It turned a used Flip monster face-down, then returned to the hand to repeat the play on a later turn.

defining_cards.name: Magical Scientist
defining_cards.why: Repeated payments of 1000 LP supplied Fusion Monsters for combat or for Catapult Turtle to tribute before they returned to the Fusion Deck.

defining_cards.name: Thousand-Eyes Restrict
defining_cards.why: It absorbed an opposing monster and stopped other monsters from attacking, buying time to reuse Flip Effects.

defining_cards.name: Vampire Lord
defining_cards.why: Pyramid Turtle could summon it from the Deck, and an opponent who destroyed it by card effect faced its return in the next Standby Phase.

defining_cards.name: Catapult Turtle
defining_cards.why: Its original effect could tribute several monsters in one turn, converting Magical Scientist's Fusion Monsters into lethal damage.

other_deck_samples.relationship: The source identifies this Spell Canceller/Ojama Trio lock as a top strategy from January 1 through April 24. Its January 1 example has 40 Main and 18 Fusion cards; all 58 still meet the April 22 Goblin whitelist and copy limits.
